niche: a grower-owned dryland barley breeding company whose nominations to an independent high-rainfall trial series keep coming in under its own trial figures: the shortfall split between the luck that got each line picked, a benchmark variety that gains more per millimetre of season water than the company's lines, and lodging losses that grow at the series' sites, then this year's Stage 3 lines re-ranked for the 2027 nominations with the chance that a nominee meets the seed partner's uptake standard
analyst_test: The careful but hurried pass puts the whole shortfall down to regression to the mean, scales the company's own high-rainfall index by the ratio the past nominees realised and nominates the same raw top three at a smaller figure, because that one story reconciles the average gap; it never estimates how much the benchmark gains per millimetre against each line, what lodging costs each line at the series' sites, or how widely two realised seasons scatter around an expected advantage, so its split of the gap, most of its line-by-line figures, its three nominations and its chance of meeting the standard are all off.
domain_test: Every result is a statistical object of selective inference on a staged screening record: the selection bias of lines picked on noisy means, estimated from the whole unselected cohort; a random-slope response carried to a target set of environments; a loss per unit of a scored trait estimated within line and trial; a decomposition that closes on two fixed means; and a posterior predictive probability for a realised two-season mean with a shared reference; swap the nouns for a sales pipeline or a hospital league table and there is no replicated plot layout, no benchmark entry in every trial, no season water and no staged advancement to estimate any of them from.
layer1: line codes renamed at promotion (stage code to release code) across entry lists
two plot-export layouts across a harvest-system change
plot weights at field moisture with a moisture reading
trial sites whose rainfall and irrigation sit in separate files
duplicate plot rows from re-weighed samples
stakeholder_role: the breeding company's head of breeding, who signs the 2027 nominations to the high-rainfall series

spine.entity: one trial plot at harvest (harvested or abandoned)

world.geography: Australia (western Victoria: the Mallee, the Wimmera and the south-west high-rainfall zone)
world.org_type: a grower-owned barley breeding company and the independent variety trial series its lines are nominated to

driver: Candidates picked each year on a noisy internal score keep underdelivering on an outside yardstick for three separate reasons that each have to be estimated from the whole internal record (the luck that got them picked, which shrinks by how much each was observed; a reference unit that gains more than they do along a condition the outside yardstick sits far up; and a recorded weakness whose cost grows there), so the gap between the two means is split into those parts and closes, the next picks are rebuilt from all three, and the chance of clearing the outside bar comes from the spread of realised results around the expectation with the reference shared, not from the spread of the estimate.
driver_concrete: Banyena's nominations to the High Rainfall Barley Series promised about ten per cent over the benchmark Byaduk on the breeder's own high-rainfall index and realised about one: part is selection on noisy Stage 3 means (lines with one Stage 3 season shrink more than lines with two, the prior taken from the whole Stage 1 cohort), part is Byaduk gaining more yield per millimetre of season water than Banyena's dryland-bred lines at series sites far wetter than the programme's, and part is lodging, whose loss per score unit is estimated within line and trial and carried to the series' lodging pressure; the 2027 nominations are the three Stage 3 lines highest on all three together, and the chance that at least one meets the 103 per cent two-season standard is read from simulated seasons that share Byaduk and the weather.
stump: A careful but hurried solver reproduces the shortfall, calls it regression to the mean, fits realised on promised across the past nominees and nominates the top three of the breeder's own high-rainfall index at the scaled figure; the step that lands it there is stopping at the first account that reconciles the average, when the shortfall differs line by line with how little water response and how much lodging each line carries, so the scaled index keeps weak-strawed and water-unresponsive lines on the list.
results: R1 the conformed trial record and the shortfall on the completed nominations (promised against realised); R2 the part of the shortfall that is selection on noisy means; R3 the part that is the benchmark's larger gain per millimetre of season water; R4 the part that is lodging at the series' sites; R5 the bridge closed with what stays unexplained and its range; R6 the corrected prediction's error on the past nominees against the breeder's index; R7 every 2026 Stage 3 line's expected advantage in the 2027 and 2028 series with an 80 per cent band; R8 each nominee's chance of meeting the 103 per cent standard and the chance at least one does; R9 the three nominations in order and the lines they displace
one_fact_test: The most useful single sentence is 'the benchmark gains more yield per millimetre of season water than our lines': it rescues R3 and moves R7 part of the way, 2 of 9 results; the selection split, the lodging loss, the closed bridge, the validation and the chance of meeting the standard each still need their own work.
